title: Parameter-product closure kernels and flat extension
statement:
Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian regular ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme], let $r\ge0$, let $a,z_1,\ldots,z_r\in C$, and assume that in each local ring $C_y$ the nonunit members of this indexed list occur at distinct positions in a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Fix $e\ge1$, and put $P=\prod_{j=1}^r z_j$, $f=a^eP$, with empty product $1$. Let $T=\operatorname{Spec}((C/(f))[1/a])\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ be the locally closed immersion of $V(f)$ restricted to $D(a)$. Its scheme-theoretic closure [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] is $V(P)$, with ideal
$$K=\ker(C\to(C/(f))[1/a])=\{h\in C:\exists n\ge0,\ a^nh\in(f)\}=(P).$$
For every prime $y$ and $S=C_y$ one has
$$KS=\{h\in S:\exists n\ge0,\ a^nh\in fS\}=PS.$$
Here quotient and localization use the images of $a,f$ in the corresponding rings. More generally, for any flat homomorphism $C\to E$ (meaning $E$ is a flat $C$-module), write $a_E,f_E,P_E$ for their images. Then
$$\ker(E\to(E/(f_E))[1/a_E])=KE=P_EE,$$
and the closure of $T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}C}\operatorname{Spec}E$ in $\operatorname{Spec}E$ is $V(P_E)$. These equalities concern ideals and closed subschemes, not just underlying closed sets. No regularity or Noetherian hypothesis on $E$ is required. In particular, if $C$ is an $A$-algebra and $B_0$ is a flat $A$-algebra, the same kernel formula holds for $E=C\otimes_A B_0$, with the canonical images of $a,f,P$.

The parameter-product saturation is the explicit UFD consequence used in ILO VIII 4.1.8 and 4.2.9.

proof.text: For any commutative ring $R$, ideal $I$ and $b\in R$, apply the fraction equivalence in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] to $M=R/I$ and the powers of $b$. The class of $h$ maps to zero in $(R/I)[1/b]$ exactly when $b^nh\in I$ for some $n\ge0$, since the kernel of $R\to R/I$ is $I$ by [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. This proves the displayed kernel-as-saturation description both over $C$ and over each $S=C_y$, without any regularity assumption.

source.place: Section 00CM, fraction equivalence and localization map, Definition 07JZ (definition-localization-module); quotient construction.

proof.text: Fix $y$ and $S=C_y$. Regularity means precisely that $S$ is regular local. Permute a parameter system to put all nonunit members of $(a,z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ first. Apply part (b) of [lem-sfb-transverse-prime-ideal-parameters] to that list and its sublist of nonunit $z_j$. It gives $PS=\bigcap_{z_j\notin S^\times}(z_j)S$, and these coordinate ideals, together with $(a)S$ if $a$ is a nonunit, are incomparable primes. Unit $z_j$ do not change the product ideal. In particular $a\notin(z_j)S$ for every nonunit $z_j$: for unit $a$ this holds because the ideal is proper; otherwise it follows from incomparability. If $a^nh\in fS\subseteq PS$, primality applied repeatedly gives $h\in(z_j)S$ for every such $j$, hence $h\in PS$. Conversely $h=Pv$ implies $a^eh=fv\in fS$. Therefore the saturation over $S$ is $PS$. If there are no nonunit $z_j$, the empty intersection is $S$ and the same converse proves the assertion.

proof.text: If $h\in K$, Step 1 gives $a^nh\in(f)$, and Step 2 gives $h/1\in PS$ for every $S=C_y$, in particular at every maximal ideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-membership-at-maximal-localizations] to $J=(P)$ to obtain $h\in(P)$. Conversely $h=Pv$ gives $a^eh=fv$, so $h\in K$. Thus $K=(P)$, and extending this equality to $S$ gives $KS=PS$, which by Steps 1--2 is also the local saturation. This proves all local equalities without assuming that saturation commutes with localization.

source.place: Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local), applied to the class of h in C/(P).

proof.text: Put $Q=C/(f)$ and $L=Q[1/a]$. Step 3 says the $C$-module sequence $0\to K\to C\to L$ is exact. Tensor it with the flat $C$-module $E$ using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. The image of $E\otimes_CK\to E\otimes_CC=E$ consists of finite sums $\sum u_i k_i$, hence is exactly $KE$. Its kernel conclusion is therefore $\ker(E\to E\otimes_CL)=KE$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change], $D=E\otimes_CQ=E/(f_E)$. The tensor associativity identification $E\otimes_CL=D\otimes_QL$ sends $u\otimes(q/a^n)$ to $(u\otimes q)/a_E^n$: [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], applied to $Q\to L$ and $Q\to D$, identifies its target with $D[1/a_E]$. Both comparisons send $u\otimes1$ to the class of $u$, so the map whose kernel was just computed is exactly $E\to(E/(f_E))[1/a_E]$. Since $K=(P)$, its kernel is $KE=(P_E)$. No property of $E$ beyond its flatness was used.

source.place: Tags 00HD (lemma-flat), 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact); Section 00CM, universal property of localization. Algebraic proof of morphisms.tex Tag 081I (lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image) in this affine case.

proof.text: For a ring map $R\to H$, inverse images of basic opens $D(c)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ are the spectra $\operatorname{Spec}(H[1/c])$. They are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact]. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}H\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is quasi-compact (check on this affine basis). By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel], with the global affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$, its scheme-theoretic image has ideal exactly $\ker(R\to H)$; global sections and the map are identified by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Apply this first to $C\to L$: Step 3 gives the closed subscheme $V(P)$. Apply it also to $E\to(E/(f_E))[1/a_E]$: Step 4 gives $V(P_E)$. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and the actual ring comparison in Step 4 identify this second source, with its map to $\operatorname{Spec}E$, with $T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}C}\operatorname{Spec}E$. These images are the closures by [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], because the maps are the locally closed immersions specified in the statement. Thus the conclusions are equalities of ideals and of closed subschemes.

source.place: morphisms.tex Tags 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image), 056A (example-scheme-theoretic-image); affine scheme fibre products and basic-open localizations.

proof.text: Finally suppose $A\to C$ and $B_0$ is flat over $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change], $C\otimes_A B_0$ is flat as a $C$-module through $c\mapsto c\otimes1$. Apply Steps 4--5 to precisely this map. They give the stated tensor-base kernel formula and closure, with $a,f,P$ sent to $a\otimes1,f\otimes1,P\otimes1$.
